extra.message: The 'threshold' query-string parameter (app/routes/allocations.js, req.query.threshold) is concatenated directly into a MongoDB $where clause, which executes as raw JavaScript on the server. An attacker can supply a payload like `1'; return true; var x='` to break out of the string literal and inject arbitrary JS into the query (e.g. exfiltrate all records, cause a DoS with an infinite loop). No sanitization/whitelisting of 'threshold' is performed before interpolation.

cwe: CWE-943: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements in Data Query Logic (NoSQL Injection)

extra.message: The URL fetched via needle.get() is built entirely from unvalidated user-controlled query parameters 'url' and 'symbol' (req.query.url + req.query.symbol). An attacker can point this at internal services (e.g. http://169.254.169.254/, internal admin endpoints, localhost ports) and have the server fetch them, with the response body reflected back in the HTTP response. This is a classic Server-Side Request Forgery.

The '/learn' route redirects to a URL taken directly from req.query.url with no validation against an allow-list or same-origin check. An attacker can craft a link like /learn?url=https://evil.example.com to redirect authenticated users to a phishing site, abusing trust in the application's domain.

cwe: CWE-601: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site ('Open Redirect')

extra.message: req.body.preTax, req.body.afterTax and req.body.roth are passed directly into eval(), executing attacker-supplied text as JavaScript on the server. A payload such as `require('child_process').execSync('id')` (or any JS expression) submitted in the 'preTax' form field will execute with full server-side privileges, resulting in remote code execution.

cwe: CWE-95: Improper Neutralization of Directives in Dynamically Evaluated Code ('Eval Injection')

extra.message: The 'userId' used to look up allocation/financial data is taken directly from the URL path parameter (req.params.userId) instead of the authenticated session (req.session.userId). Any logged-in user can view any other user's private financial allocations by changing the userId in the URL (e.g. GET /allocations/2), with only an 'isLoggedIn' check and no ownership/authorization check. The commented-out code confirms the intended fix (use req.session.userId) was disabled.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: The /benefits GET and POST routes are only guarded by 'isLoggedIn', not by the 'isAdmin' middleware (the correct check is present but commented out below). Since benefitsHandler.updateBenefits (app/routes/benefits.js) accepts an arbitrary 'userId' in the POST body and updates that user's benefitStartDate with no role check, any authenticated non-admin user can view the full user list and modify any other user's benefits data.

displayProfile renders 'doc' (containing lastName, ssn, dob, bankAcc, bankRouting, address — all persisted verbatim from user-supplied req.body in profile-dao.js updateUser) directly into the 'profile' template. Swig's global autoescape is disabled (server.js autoescape: false), and app/views/profile.html interpolates these fields unescaped into HTML attribute values (e.g. value="{{address}}"). An attacker can submit an address such as `"><script>alert(document.cookie)</script>` via POST /profile to store a stored XSS payload that executes whenever the profile page is viewed.

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

extra.message: On bank-routing validation failure, 'firstNameSafeString' is set to the raw, unsanitized 'firstName' from req.body and rendered back into app/views/profile.html line 78 inside an href attribute (`<a href="{{firstNameSafeString}}">`) with autoescape disabled. An attacker-supplied firstName such as `javascript:alert(document.cookie)` or `" onclick="alert(1)` results in script execution when the link is used, despite the misleading variable name suggesting it is sanitized.

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

extra.message: The Express session signing secret ('cookieSecret') and the symmetric encryption key ('cryptoKey') are hardcoded string literals committed to source control rather than loaded from a secrets manager or environment variable. Anyone with source access can forge session cookies or decrypt data encrypted with this key.

addUser stores the user's password field verbatim from the request with no hashing (bcrypt.hashSync is present in a comment but not used). validateLogin (line 61) then compares passwords with a plain '===' string comparison against this plaintext value. A database compromise or backup leak exposes every user's password in cleartext, and login is also vulnerable to a non-constant-time comparison timing side-channel.

The bank-routing validation regex `/([0-9]+)+\#/` uses a nested quantifier (a '+' repetition around a group that itself ends in '+'), causing catastrophic backtracking on crafted input such as a long run of digits with no trailing '#' (e.g. '111111111111111111111111111111!'). This is reachable directly from POST /profile via the 'bankRouting' field and can hang the Node.js event loop, denying service to all users. The developer's own comment confirms this is the vulnerable (unfixed) version of the regex.

On successful login, req.session.userId is set on the existing session without first calling req.session.regenerate(). A session ID obtained by an attacker before authentication (e.g. via an insecure network or session ID fixation) remains valid and gains the victim's privileges after they log in, since the session ID itself never changes.

The express-session configuration sets no 'cookie.httpOnly', no 'cookie.secure', no 'maxAge', and uses the default cookie name (the hardening options are present only as comments). Without httpOnly, a successful XSS (see CWE-79 findings) can read the session cookie via document.cookie and exfiltrate it; without 'secure', the cookie can be transmitted over plain HTTP.

All Helmet-based security headers (clickjacking protection via frameguard, CSP, HSTS, disabling x-powered-by, no-sniff) are commented out and never applied. The application discloses the 'X-Powered-By: Express' header and can be embedded in a hostile iframe for clickjacking, with no Content-Security-Policy to mitigate XSS impact.

The application is served over plain HTTP (http.createServer) rather than HTTPS; the TLS server setup is present but fully commented out. Session cookies, passwords, and SSNs/bank details submitted via the profile form are transmitted in cleartext over the network.

cwe: CWE-319: Cleartext Transmission of Sensitive Information

extra.message: The user-supplied 'userName' from the login form is written directly into the application log via console.log with no CRLF/control-character encoding. An attacker can include newline characters in the username field to forge additional fake log lines (log injection / log forging), and the value is also included raw in the log output. The surrounding comment documents the intended ESAPI-based encoding fix that is not applied.

cwe: CWE-117: Improper Output Neutralization for Logs

extra.message: PASS_RE = /^.{1,20}$/ accepts any password of 1-20 characters with no complexity requirement (a stronger regex requiring digits, upper- and lower-case letters is present in a comment but unused). This allows trivially weak passwords like 'a', making accounts easy to brute-force.
